paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy, Li et al. (2016) identified a recurrent de novo heterozygous missense mutation (c.1999G-A; V667I) in the GRIN2D gene, found by exome and candidate panel sequencing. The V667I substitution lies in the M3 transmembrane domain involved in channel gating. Functional studies showed a gain-of-function effect: the mutation increased glutamate and glycine potency 2-fold, increased channel open probability 6-fold, reduced receptor sensitivity to endogenous negative modulators such as extracellular protons, and prolonged the deactivation time course after glutamate removal. Transfection of cultured neurons with mutant human GRIN2D cDNA led to dendritic swelling and neuronal cell death, suggestive of excitotoxicity mediated by NMDA receptor overactivation.

paragraphs.text: By whole-exome sequencing in 3 unrelated patients with severe developmental delay and intractable epilepsy, Tsuchida et al. (2018) identified novel heterozygous missense variants in the GRIN2D gene. All altered residues were highly conserved across vertebrates and among the 4 GluN2 subunits. Structural consideration indicated that all 3 variants probably impair GluN2D function, either by affecting intersubunit interaction or by altering channel gating activity.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) evaluated the sensitivity of the mutant NMDA receptors to FDA-approved NMDA receptor antagonists and, based on the results, administered oral memantine to both patients, with mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development. The older proband subsequently developed refractory status epilepticus that showed dramatic electroclinical improvement upon treatment with ketamine and magnesium.

paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy (DEE46), Li et al. (2016) identified a recurrent de novo heterozygous c.1999G-A transition in the GRIN2D gene, resulting in a val667-to-ile (V667I) substitution in the M3 transmembrane domain. Functional studies showed that the mutation caused a gain of function, increasing glutamate and glycine potency 2-fold and channel open probability 6-fold, reducing sensitivity to extracellular protons, and prolonging deactivation; expression in cultured neurons led to dendritic swelling and neuronal cell death.

agent.process_note: Both papers were available as abstracts only, and I read both in full. Li et al. (2016) gave the V667I variant, its de novo heterozygous status, the functional data and the response to treatment. Tsuchida et al. (2018) reported 3 more patients, but its abstract does not name their variants, so they could not be listed as allelic variants. Neither abstract gives patient ages, sex, ancestry or seizure types. No reference data were supplied, so the GRIN2D MIM number and chromosome location are left out of the intro.
